# .gitignore for _APP_ -- A WHITELIST, not a list of exclusions.
#
# homerTidy overwrites this file from RepoFiles.txt. Run
#
#     homerTidy --gitignore
#
# after adding a line to RepoFiles.txt, and do not edit this file by hand.
#
# Why a whitelist. A list of exclusions is only ever as complete as the last
# time somebody remembered to add a line, and the file that gets pushed by
# accident is always the one nobody thought of. Ignoring everything and putting
# back exactly what the project names turns that around: a file dropped into the
# folder is invisible to git until it is named.
#
# Until homerTidy is run, this starter keeps the obvious hazards out.

# Ignore everything.
/*

# Put back what a new app starts with.
!/.gitignore
!/_APP_.cs
!/_APP__setup.iss
!/build_APP_.cmd
!/homerFinish.cmd
!/installModels.cmd
!/installOllama.cmd
!/installScreenReaderSupport.cmd
!/version.txt
!/RepoFiles.txt

# Never pushed, whatever RepoFiles.txt says: private notes, maintainer scripts,
# logs, and anything a build makes.
*.exe
*.log
*.obj
*.pdb
Version.cs
__pycache__/
create*Repo.cmd
create*Repo.ps1
notes/
self.htm
self.md
tagRelease.cmd
tagRelease.ps1
version.py
logs/
